cases.title: invalid/table/append-with-dotted-keys-01.toml
cases.input:
# First a.b.c defines a table: a.b.c = {z=9}
#
# Then we define a.b.c.t = "str" to add a str to the above table, making it:
#
#   a.b.c = {z=9, t="..."}
#
# While this makes sense, logically, it was decided this is not valid TOML as
# it's too confusing/convoluted.
# 
# See: https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/issues/846
#      https://github.com/toml-lang/toml/pull/859

[a.b.c]
  z = 9

[a]
  b.c.t = "Using dotted keys to add to [a.b.c] after explicitly defining it above is not allowed"

cases.title: invalid/table/array-implicit.toml
cases.input:
# This test is a bit tricky. It should fail because the first use of
# `[[albums.songs]]` without first declaring `albums` implies that `albums`
# must be a table. The alternative would be quite weird. Namely, it wouldn't
# comply with the TOML spec: "Each double-bracketed sub-table will belong to 
# the most *recently* defined table element *above* it."
#
# This is in contrast to the *valid* test, table-array-implicit where
# `[[albums.songs]]` works by itself, so long as `[[albums]]` isn't declared
# later. (Although, `[albums]` could be.)
[[albums.songs]]
name = "Glory Days"

[[albums]]
name = "Born in the USA"

cases.title: Basic string with escape
cases.paragraph: Basic strings are surrounded by quotation marks. Escapes include \n, \t, \", \\, \uXXXX.

cases.title: Multiline basic string
cases.paragraph: Multiline basic strings are surrounded by three quotation marks.

cases.title: Integer with underscores
cases.paragraph: Underscores may be used to enhance readability of integers.

cases.title: Fractional float
cases.paragraph: A float consists of an integer part followed by a fractional part and/or an exponent part.

cases.title: Trailing commas in arrays are allowed in 1.0
cases.paragraph: Arrays can span multiple lines. A terminating comma (also called trailing comma) is permitted.

cases.title: Array of tables
cases.paragraph: Double brackets declare an array of tables.

cases.title: Offset date-time
cases.notes: Decoded type is implementation-defined (datetime vs string). Accept-only.

cases.title: Trailing commas in inline tables are invalid in 1.0
cases.paragraph: No newlines are allowed between the curly braces unless they are valid within a value. Trailing commas are not permitted in 1.0 inline tables.

cases.title: A table cannot be defined twice
cases.paragraph: Defining a table twice is invalid.

cases.title: Spaces in a bare key are invalid
cases.paragraph: Bare keys may only contain ASCII letters, ASCII digits, underscores, and dashes.

cases.title: Boolean True is invalid
cases.paragraph: Booleans are true or false. Always lowercase.
